summary_support.quote: - **Side I:** Build **exactly 1 building** of your choice, of size up to the action's strength. Pay **2 money per space** (cost = size × 2) into the supply before placing. Available: kiosk (size 1), pavilion (size 1), standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), and the Petting Zoo (special enclosure, size 3; maximum 1 per zoo — other buildings can be built more than once).

- **Placement rules:** build adjacent to an existing building (at least 1 edge touching); your **first building** must instead have at least 1 space on a border space of your zoo map. Build only on empty spaces; buildings may not extend beyond the map, overlap buildings, or cover water/rock spaces. Spaces with the restricted icon require the upgraded Build action. A kiosk must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk (at least 2 spaces between kiosks). If you cannot legally build the desired building, you must choose a different building. Build standard enclosures **empty side up** (yellow edge, showing the size); the Petting Zoo is the same on both sides. Covering a placement-bonus space grants that bonus immediately, once. Each pavilion immediately (and only once) increases your zoo's appeal by 1; kiosks grant income in every break; enclosures house animals.

- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

paired_records.question: Can money or other bonuses gained during an action pay for a later building, animal or association task in that action? How do immediate and after-finishing effects and simultaneous effects differ?

reader_a.answer_quote: Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, can be used in later steps of that same action. Pay each item before receiving that item's own benefit, and an animal's full cost must be payable before its money-gain effect pays out. Immediate effects resolve as they occur; ‘after finishing’ effects wait until the whole action and Action-card movement are complete. If effects are simultaneous, the owning player chooses their order.

summary_support.quote: **X-tokens.** You may use X-tokens to increase an action's strength: each token spent adds +1 strength, then returns to the supply. You may spend any number in one action (for some actions, strength above 5 no longer improves the action). You can never hold more than 5 X-tokens. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action; resolve its items one at a time. You must pay each item before receiving its own benefits. You set the strength **before** performing the action — X-tokens gained while performing an action cannot boost that same action.
**"After finishing" effects.** If a card effect says "after finishing" your action, complete the action — including moving the Action cards — before executing the effect.

- **Side II:** Build **as many different buildings as you like** with a **maximum total size equal to the strength** — but never 2 identical buildings in the same Build action. Newly available: **Large Bird Aviary** and **Reptile House** (special enclosures, both size 5, maximum 1 each per zoo, both sides the same). When you build the Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary you may immediately — and only once per building — move **all suitable animals that fit** from standard enclosures into it, choosing separately for each. Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

5. **Execute effects:** advance your Appeal counter by the amount shown; some animals also give conservation points or reputation. "After finishing" effects wait until the entire Animals action is done; all other effects execute immediately, even before playing another Animal card (likewise effects on other cards triggered by the play). If multiple effects are simultaneous, you choose the order.

summary_support.quote: - **Increase reputation (strength 2):** increase your zoo's reputation by **2**, taking any track bonuses you reach.

If every zoo currently on the board is one you already have, or you cannot place it, you cannot perform this task. Each partner zoo reduces the cost of Animal cards from its continent by 3 money per continent icon, provides 1 icon of that continent (usable for card effects and conservation projects), and some Animal cards require one.

- **Gain university (strength 4):** take a university from the Association board onto the lowest available university space and take its covered-space bonus immediately. **Also gain the reputation printed on the university tile immediately.** You cannot take a duplicate university. - **Conservation project work (strength 5):** either support a conservation project already in play, or play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately. A new card goes on the leftmost space above the Association board, pushing existing cards one place right. Depending on player count there can only be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players); if the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card and return any player tokens on it to their owners' supplies (not to their zoo maps). **The Base Conservation Projects below the board never move and are never replenished**, even when fully supported.

independent_scope_reason.change: Require the six break steps in order and the explicitly named detailed subquestions; move restock quantities/exclusions and income-type composition order to context.
independent_scope_reason.why: The literal prompt asks break steps in order, hand limit, kiosk qualifying neighbors, and income order/refill when several players take display cards. The latter is the affected-player ordering, not an added appeal/kiosk/Sponsor suborder demand. Restock is the named Association-board step; its exact per-kind quantities and all-owned exception are not separately requested. Both answers give the six steps and all named details. This is a scope correction, not a claim that restocking rules are optional or different.

paired_records.paired_reason: Both give all six break steps in order, numerical hand limits, all qualifying kiosk neighbors with the empty-standard/special distinction, and affected-player clockwise display-income order plus between-player refill. The question asks step order, not every restocking subrule or the composition/order of income types; those extra index demands are context.

reader_a.answer_quote: Break steps are: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the hand-limit university); clear Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and restock partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, compact and refill; take income; reset the Break token. A kiosk earns 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; an empty standard enclosure does not qualify, while an empty special enclosure does. Income is appeal-based, then kiosk income, then Sponsor/map break income. If multiple players take display cards during income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them) and refill after each player's income before the next chooses.

**When more than one player receives a display card during break income, resolve those players clockwise starting with the break initiator (or the first affected player clockwise from them). Refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.** This ordering and the between-player refill apply together.
6. **Break track:** return the Break token to the starting space for your player count. Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

summary_support.quote: 1. **Hand card limit:** discard cards of your choice down to your hand limit — normally 3, or 5 with a particular university.
2. **Tokens on Action cards:** return any Multiplier, Venom, and/or Constriction tokens on your Action cards to the supply; they no longer have any effect.

3. **Association board:** return all your association workers to your notepad (active again — all tasks are again available at 1 worker). **Restock one tile of each partner-zoo continent and each university kind**, except kinds **already owned by every player**; do not add duplicate available tiles.
4. **Replenish display:** discard the two bottom cards of the display (folders 1 and 2), move the remaining cards down, and refill the display.

5. **Take income** (when multiple players take display cards, **refill the display after each player**; usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, begin with the player who initiated the break — or the affected player closest to them — and proceed clockwise):
- a. Money according to your zoo's **appeal** (the amount printed next to your counter on the Appeal track; e.g., space 7 pays 11 money).

- b. **Kiosk income:** for each kiosk, take 1 money per unique building, special enclosure, **occupied** standard enclosure, and pavilion adjacent to it (sharing at least one side of a space). An empty standard enclosure provides no income, but an empty special enclosure does.
- c. All income marked with the break-income icon on your Sponsor cards and on your **activated** zoo-map bonuses (those uncovered by supporting conservation projects).

**When more than one player receives a display card during break income, resolve those players clockwise starting with the break initiator (or the first affected player clockwise from them). Refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.** This ordering and the between-player refill apply together.
6. **Break track:** return the Break token to the starting space for your player count. Play then continues clockwise with the next player.

reader_a.answer_quote: At 2 conservation, choose either an Action-card upgrade or an additional active association worker. At 5 and 8, choose 5 money or the Bonus token next to that space (the money option remains when tokens are gone). The first time anyone reaches 10, every player discards one Final Scoring card face down under the remaining pile; if no one reaches 10 before game end, all do so before scoring. Check for the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when appeal and conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained on another player's turn waits until the end of your turn or a break. Finish the triggering turn; if triggered on a turn, every other player takes one more turn; if during a break, every player takes one more. Each Final Scoring card can award at most 4 conservation. Victory Points equal appeal minus the lowest appeal value in the scoring area containing your conservation counter; highest positive total wins, with ties broken by most supported projects, then shared victory.

summary_support.quote: **End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

summary_support.quote: - **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.

- **5 and 8 conservation points:** take either 5 money or one of the Bonus tokens next to that space (execute immediately; a taken Bonus token is then removed from the game). The 5-money option remains even after both Bonus tokens are gone.

- **10 conservation points:** the first time any player reaches or exceeds 10, **all players** choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile). If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.

**End of the game.** Check **at the end of your own turn or during a break**. If your Conservation counter and Appeal counter are **in the same scoring area, or pass one another**, the end of the game is triggered. A *scoring area* is one space on the Conservation track together with the adjacent spaces on the Appeal track. Appeal gained during another player's turn (for example from Polar Bear Exhibit) waits until the end of your own turn or a break to trigger the end, unless someone else triggers it first. The triggering player completes their turn and all other players take **one more turn**; if the end is triggered during a break, **all** players take one more turn.

1. Score your Final Scoring card(s) and all your cards with the end-of-game icon. Each Final Scoring card can grant up to 4 additional conservation points (by table or text, counting your universities, the cards in front of you, and their icons); you can never gain more than **4 conservation points from a single Final Scoring card**.

2. Compute Victory Points: look at the scoring area where your Conservation counter is located and find the **lowest Appeal value in that scoring area** — this is your **Target Number**. **Victory Points = your Appeal value − your Target Number.**

3. The player with the highest positive Victory Point total wins. **Tiebreaker:** the tied player who supported the most conservation projects wins (count the player tokens removed from the left side of the zoo map). If still tied, the tied players share the victory.

reader_a.answer_quote: When an Action-card upgrade is earned, flip one card of your choice from side I to side II in its current slot. There are **4 ways to upgrade** an Action card: on the Conservation track, on the Reputation track, and when you gain your second partner zoo or your second partner university. summary_support.quote: - **Side II:** Perform **one or more different** association tasks with one action (1 or 2 of your workers per task, as above). The **total value** of the tasks may not exceed your action's strength (it may be less). Tasks resolve in sequence: workers or other bonuses gained from an earlier task may be used on a later task in this same action. paired_records.question: Where are Constriction 1/2 tokens placed, can they stack, how do they change strength and multiplied actions, and when are they removed?

independent_scope_reason.change: The neutral index matches the actual requested subject matter.
independent_scope_reason.why: Each requested part was assessed semantically within this answer; extra key context was not independently demanded.

paired_records.paired_reason: Both place one at five or two at four/five, prohibit stacking and return duplicates, subtract two from every multiplied execution, allow X-token restoration and remove used/unused tokens at the right times. A's added track-based selection matches the snapshot.

reader_a.answer_quote: Constriction targets all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Give Constriction 1 to a zoo ahead on one track and 2 to one ahead on both. Place tokens on the affected player's highest-slot cards: one on slot 5, or two on slots 4 and 5; never stack two on one card, returning duplicates. Each token reduces that action's strength by 2, including each execution of a multiplied action; X-tokens can restore strength. Return a token after its card is used, or without effect at the break.

reader_a.answer_quote: Hypnosis lets you choose an affected player among those tied for highest appeal; if you target yourself, it has no effect. Venom and Constriction tokens on the targeted card affect the copied action and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally.

Build the buildings one after the other, paying for each separately before placing it; take placement bonuses before building the next building, but hold "after finishing" bonuses until the whole Build action is complete. Side II also lets you build on the restricted-icon spaces, so you can completely cover your zoo map: if you cover every space except water and rock spaces (by any effect, not just the Build action), immediately gain **7 appeal**. Unique buildings can never be built with this action — they only come into play via their Sponsor cards.

reader_a.answer_quote: Venom places up to X tokens on the affected player's lowest-slot cards, one token per card; duplicates return to supply. If any Venom token remains at turn end, pay 2 money; if unable, undo the turn and choose another action, and you cannot avoid the fee by spending all money. Unused Venom tokens expire at the next break.
